title: Open Ruy Lopez
intro: Black takes on e4 with 5...Nxe4. Strike in the centre with 6.d4, push 8.dxe5 against ...d5, and answer 6...exd4 with Re1.
variation: e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1b5 a7a6 b5a4 g8f6 e1g1 f6e4

lessons.title: The Open main line
lessons.summary: Open the centre with 6.d4 and drive Black back with 8.dxe5.

steps.text: In the Open Variation, Black captures the e4 pawn with 5...Nxe4. Black's king is still in the middle, so White opens the centre at once.

steps.ifWrong: Play 6.d4 to open lines against Black's uncastled king.

feedback.f1e1: 6.Re1 lets Black reply 6...Nc5 7.Bxc6 dxc6 and trade off your bishop.

steps.text: Black drives the bishop away with 6...b5.
Keep the bishop on the a2-g8 diagonal.
steps.ifRight: From b3 the bishop eyes d5 and f7.

steps.text: Black supports the e4 knight with 7...d5.
Open the e-file and drive Black's pieces back.
steps.hint: Capture on e5 with your d-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8.dxe5 to claim the d4 square and attack d5.
steps.ifRight: Notice how d5 is now vulnerable and your pieces have open lines.

steps.text: Black defends d5 with 8...Be6. Play the main move to reinforce d4 and keep the queenside flexible.
steps.hint: Push the c-pawn one square to prepare Bc2 and Nbd2.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9.c3 (or 9.Nbd2 or 9.Be3): c3 prepares Bc2 and guards d4.
steps.ifRight: Next come Nbd2, Bc2 and Re1, pressuring Black's centre.

lessons.title: Punishing 6...exd4
lessons.summary: Pin the knight along the e-file with 7.Re1.

steps.text: A common club mistake is 6...exd4, opening the e-file while Black's king is still on e8.
Pin the e4 knight to the king at once.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Re1 to pin the knight and win material or the initiative.
steps.ifRight: Black must protect the pinned knight immediately.

steps.text: Win back the d4 pawn and attack the pinned c6 knight.
steps.hint: Capture on d4 with your knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8.Nxd4: now c6 is attacked twice and pinned to the king.
steps.ifRight: White has a crushing attack down the e-file and along the a4-e8 diagonal.

steps.text: Black unpins with 8...Bd7. Win a piece or pile up pressure with a sharp capture.
steps.hint: The c6 knight and the e4 knight are both pinned. Take on c6 or hit e4 with f3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9.Bxc6 (or 9.Nxc6 or 9.f3): Black's pinned pieces cannot hold everything.
steps.ifRight: White wins material while Black's king is stuck on e8.

steps.text: What if Black tries 7...f5 to hold the knight on e4?
steps.hint: Capture on d4 with the knight, piling up on c6 and f5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8.Nxd4 to attack c6 and f5 while Black's king is stuck on e8.

lessons.title: Pressing the Open Ruy Lopez
lessons.summary: Challenge e4 with Nbd2 and tuck the bishop on c2.

steps.text: In the Open Ruy Lopez, Black's queenside pawns on a6 and b5 are pushed forward and can be weak, while the e4 knight can be challenged.
Finish developing your queenside and prepare to challenge e4.
steps.hint: Develop the b1 knight to d2.
steps.ifWrong: Play 10.Nbd2 to challenge the active e4 knight and connect your rooks.
steps.ifRight: If Black trades on d2, Bxd2 keeps your pieces active.

steps.text: Step the Spanish bishop out of the way of ...Nc5 and ...Na5.
steps.hint: Tuck the bishop back to c2.
steps.ifWrong: Play 11.Bc2 so the bishop eyes e4 and h7 and stays safe from ...Nc5.
steps.ifRight: White pressures e4 and prepares Qe2 or Nb3.

steps.text: Black steps back with 11...Nc5 to avoid trades. Fight for the strong d4 outpost.
steps.hint: Move one of your knights to b3 or d4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 12.Nb3 (or 12.Nd4) to control the dark squares in front of Black's pawns.
steps.ifRight: White controls c5 and d4 with a strong positional bind.

steps.text: What if Black trades knights with 11...Nxd2?
steps.hint: Recapture with the bishop or queen, aiming towards h7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 12.Bxd2 (or 12.Qxd2): both keep your attack on the kingside alive.
steps.ifRight: White prepares Qd3, threatening kingside pressure.
